November 19, 2026 | 9:07 am CST
Construction firm completes mass timber installation at Brooklyn Public Library
The library is Shawmut’s third project for BPL and its first cross-laminated timber building in New York.

BROOKYLN, N.Y. — Shawmut Design and Construction completed the mass timber installation for Brooklyn Public Library’s (BPL) new Canarsie Library, one of New York City’s first public mass timber buildings. The structure includes over 8,000 square feet of mass timber, 38 cross-laminated timber (CLT) panels, 169 glulam beams, and 46 glulam columns.

“Mass timber lets us build faster and with far less disruption, which matters on a busy street like Rockaway Parkway,” said Joe Boyle, project executive at Shawmut. “We brought what we’ve learned on mass timber projects across the country to our first in New York, and that experience mattered most where the glass meets the timber. Because the curtain wall attaches directly to the structure, the wood isn’t hidden behind finishes. It’s what people will see from the street and from inside the library.”

Making that connection work took planning well before the first panel arrived. Mercer Mass Timber, the project’s supplier, joined early in design to detail the structural connections, and Shawmut modeled the full building in 3D and built a 16-by-13-foot façade mockup on Long Island to test the assembly before fabrication began. Shawmut’s quality assurance plan protected the exposed wood with plywood barricades and other breathable materials instead of conventional protective wraps, which are too impermeable for cross-laminated timber.
In all, the installation required five deliveries, about 300 crane picks, and 17 ironworkers.

“A long-time partner of the Library, Shawmut Design and Construction is helping us realize our vision to create environmentally friendly, modern, and inspiring spaces in neighborhoods all across Brooklyn,” said Linda E. Johnson, president and CEO, Brooklyn Public Library.

BPL selected mass timber to reduce the building’s carbon footprint, and the library will also have on-site stormwater management, rooftop solar panels, and all-new heating, cooling, and electrical infrastructure.
Since New York City established its mass timber regulations in 2022, Shawmut sees the project as a test case as the city explores the material for public buildings.

The two-story, 11,000-square-foot library will double the public space of the former branch. It will have separate areas for adults, teens, and children, a flexible meeting room for up to 50 people, a public recording studio, a maker space, and an outdoor terrace. Designed by Studio Joseph, the library is expected to open in 2027.
